reviews.text:
Addendum: I won't lower my rating because the doctor is not at fault, but when we scheduled the surgery date and time, I had taken detailed notes, so I'm sure there were no mistakes. However, due to a communication error by the receptionist, I had a terrible experience. It's unbelievable, especially since my dog ​​is a senior. I had planned to let my dog ​​rest comfortably at home until the last minute, but I ended up rushing there, and I was in tears. The doctor is wonderful, but I've decided I'll think twice before entrusting such an important surgery to this hospital.


I'm always grateful for their care. While I have some concerns about the female staff, the doctor is an exceptionally good person, caring for animals, kind, knowledgeable, and highly skilled. Because of its popularity, there were times when I had to wait 1-2 hours, and sometimes even 2.5 hours. I don't want to say too much because I don't want it to get any more crowded, but I highly recommend it.

Thank you for your services every year!

I don't want to use anesthesia for teeth cleaning, so thank you for always cleaning my teeth so thoroughly.

Previously, I had my beloved Chihuahua spayed at this clinic. To put it simply, she has remained healthy without any major illnesses. I am incredibly grateful!

At the time, I was terrified of having a scalpel used on her small body and agonized over it for days. However, the doctor understood all my anxieties and treated me with such care that I felt completely at ease. My dog ​​didn't resist the surgery, and on the day of the operation, the staff warmly welcomed my beloved pet. I remember feeling completely confident entrusting my dog ​​to their care.

An important factor in my decision was the convenient location, right near Azabu-Juban Station. Furthermore, the fact that they are open on weekends is a huge plus. Even with a busy work schedule, I could easily fit appointments in, making it a great help for working pet owners.

Seeing my dog ​​wagging her tail and looking so energetic when I picked her up, I truly felt I had made the right choice in choosing Heart Animal Hospital. It's a reliable hospital where you can entrust your beloved dog with peace of mind and where they will protect her health.
My pet was injured, and even though it was a Saturday, they were able to see us without an appointment. The doctor and nurses were kind, and the treatment was appropriate, which was a great help.

Great hospital! The doctors are very kind and I've been receiving treatment here for a long time. 
As other reviews have said, it's a popular hospital, so I don't want it to get any more crowded, and to be honest, I don't want to tell anyone about it...! I highly recommend this hospital to my close friends! 

I wonder if the unfriendly woman who was at the reception desk a while ago has left? The receptionist has been replaced by a more friendly person, and I think this hospital is even better!!

All the doctors and nurses are kind and polite. The doctor sees patients alone, so if you're lucky you can be seen right away, but if it's busy you may have to wait an hour. However, since it's in Azabu, I can adjust my time by going for a walk or relaxing at a cafe with my dog, so it's not particularly inconvenient.

I've been seeing Dr. Ito for many years, but
the receptionist's attitude has been so bad that I'm considering changing hospitals.
The previous receptionist was never like that.
When I explained my condition over the phone, he coldly replied, "Yes, I see." I didn't understand his explanation, so I asked him to repeat it, but he explained it again in an irritated tone.
He's also really bad at cutting my nails, and one time I was bleeding on the way home. I haven't asked him to do my treatment since.
He's a kind doctor, but I'm disappointed with everything else outside of his consultations.

When I lived in Tokyo, I used to go to this clinic. I was worried about surgery for my senior dog, but thanks to the doctor's thorough explanation and skill, the surgery was completed successfully. He is a trustworthy doctor.

I've been using their anesthesia-free dental cleaning service.

The doctor is a very kind and gentle man, and I trust him because he always cleans my pet's teeth thoroughly.

For dental cleaning alone, the treatment is completed in about 20 minutes, and I'm impressed by his efficiency.

(This may vary depending on how busy the clinic is, so please take it as a reference only.)

The doctor recommends dental cleaning three times a year, so I visit regularly, but there's one woman in the clinic who has a bad attitude.

Last time, I dropped my pet off, and a few minutes later I received a call from the clinic. She said, "The root of a baby tooth that hasn't completely fallen out is loose and rotten, so we'll remove it while we're at it. We'll use anesthesia, so please give your pet medicine at home." She spoke so matter-of-factly, without my consent for extraction.

I was very uncomfortable with her way of speaking, which didn't give me any choice.

I told her I would consult with a different doctor and refused the extraction over the phone.

I was very worried that if the tooth was really rotten, it could have a negative impact on my pet's health. After the treatment, I went to pick up my dog ​​and asked the vet directly if the root of the baby tooth was decaying. He replied, "The baby tooth isn't decaying."
I was worried, so I asked the vet twice to confirm it wasn't decaying.
I was relieved by his answer, but I was also angry at the way the woman I spoke to on the phone had spoken in such an unsettling way.
To put it bluntly, it wasn't just an unsettling way of speaking; she was lying.
The vet's policy was that it was fine to either extract the baby tooth that hadn't completely fallen out or wait for it to fall out naturally.
He wasn't recommending one over the other; he was leaving the decision to the owner.
Of course, the other vet I see also has the same policy, so as the owner, I was waiting for it to fall out naturally without extraction. (The teeth I'm talking about here aren't large teeth like canines, but small teeth that don't need to be extracted immediately.)

I believe the doctor instructed her to call to confirm whether or not to extract the tooth, but I couldn't understand what had happened to make that woman speak to him that way...

There was an unfriendly person at the checkout counter, so I suspected that this was the woman who made the call.

I have absolutely no complaints about the doctor's personality or the treatment, and I will continue to go there, but this rating is due to that one woman.
